subject: Catalyst Health — multi-region surge & packaging concession (VP/CFO signoff requested)
messages:
From: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@catalysthealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot pricing ask — multi-region burst + packaging questions

Hi Vanessa,

Quick intro — we run patient ingestion pipelines across US regions and expect sporadic multi-region bursts over the next 12 months. We like Redwood's serving performance but need a commercial structure that covers:
- an introductory discount during the pilot (peak bursts expected month 2–4)
- waiver of the VPC/onboarding packaging surcharge for the first year
- clear conversion terms to standard committed pricing after pilot

Can you share a proposed rate card and confirm whether Redwood can grant a one-off packaging waiver? Procurement needs a commercial signoff this quarter to align budget.

Attached: our internal SOW and expected monthly token profile (CSV).

Best,
Evan Ruiz
Procurement Manager | Catalyst Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Ruiz <evan.ruiz@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing ask — multi-region burst + packaging questions

Thanks Evan — appreciate the level of detail. Quick answers up front:
- We can design a short-term pilot discount; discounts >20% require VP/CFO review.
- Packaging / VPC surcharge is waivable on a case-by-case basis (internal approval required).
- We'll propose a conversion path to a committed 18-month agreement if the pilot meets consumption thresholds.

I'll pull together a short internal exception memo and proposed banding for you (prelim numbers attached). Can you confirm: expected peak qps, whether PII-sensitive workloads will be in the VPC (yes/no), and target go/no-go date for the pilot? That will speed approvals.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial exception request: Catalyst Health — tiered multi-region surge credit

Kimberly / Marissa (cc Jonas),

Catalyst (DEAL-8942) has asked for a commercial exception for their pilot: 30% off hosted token rates for the pilot window (months 1–12) plus a full waiver of the VPC/onboarding surcharge for 12 months. They project $480k ARR on an annualized basis if converted to committed after pilot.

Why I'm asking for signoff: the requested 30% + 12-month packaging waiver exceeds standard delegation. Quick summary:
- Customer: Catalyst Health (healthcare SaaS) — US regions, some PII; they will run in our VPC for the pilot (so packaging + onboarding work estimate = $28k).
- Ask: 30% tiered discount (pilot period), packaging waiver for 12 months, contract auto-converts to 18-month committed term at standard rates on conversion.
- Revenue expectation: estimated ARR on conversion: $480k; expected pilot cost (incremental GPU/egress) estimated at ~$45k over 12 months.

Attachments: internal_exception_memo_Catalyst_DEAL-8942.docx (formal memo), pricing_model_v3.xlsx (unit economics), catalyst_pricing_request.pdf (customer SOW).

Decision requested: VP/CFO signoff for the commercial exception or directional guidance. If we need to limit exposure, suggested alternatives are listed in the memo (shorter packaging waiver, ramped discount to 22% with a 6-month packaging waiver).

I ran the deal for timing — procurement is asking to execute paperwork by 12/10. Please advise — happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through the model if useful.

Thanks,
Vanessa
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial exception request: Catalyst Health — tiered multi-region surge credit

Vanessa — reviewed the numbers and ran sensitivity against our cost model. Key points:
- If we grant 30% + 12-month packaging waiver, blended gross margin on the converted ARR drops ~10 percentage points relative to standard rate; projected COCA (cost of customer acquisition + implementation) becomes tighter.
- For risk mitigation I recommend either: (A) limit the packaging waiver to 6 months and approve a 22% pilot discount, or (B) keep 12-month waiver but cap discount at 20% and require a minimum committed ARR threshold on conversion.
- Also recommend we require: a written pilot acceptance criteria and automated conversion trigger (HubSpot deal stage and DocuSign amendment).

I attached a short sensitivity sheet in pricing_model_v3.xlsx showing scenario outcomes. If leadership wants to preserve runway, option A is the least dilutive while remaining competitive.

Kimberly
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 17:34:00 -0800
Subject: Approval: Catalyst Health concession (modified)

Thanks everyone for the clear modeling. Approve moving forward on a modified path:
- Approve 22% pilot discount (months 1–12).
- Approve packaging/VPC onboarding waiver for 6 months only.
- Conditions: pilot acceptance criteria must be signed off by Catalyst and Redwood CS, and conversion to the committed 18-month term must be implemented via DocuSign amendment (linked: https://www.docusign.com/templates/DEAL-8942-amendment).
- Finance (Jonas) — please confirm accounting treatment for the packaging waiver (deferred revenue / credit memo process) and confirm any SG&A holdbacks needed.

Vanessa: proceed to issue the term sheet to Catalyst reflecting the approved guardrails and loop in Legal for the amendment. Kimberly: update the pricing_model_v3.xlsx with the final approved scenario and push to the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8942).

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
